query: Why is learning satisfaction low for certain groups, and which factors drive it?

per_column.name: low_satisfaction_flag
per_column.rationale: Binary recoding of the outcome (satisfaction below threshold); it is a restatement of the focus variable, not a treatment or confounder.

per_column.name: tech_issue_mentions
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause of dissatisfaction extracted from open responses; a plausible driver whose effect on satisfaction is being attributed.

per_column.name: engagement_mentions
per_column.rationale: Another candidate driver surfaced from text; treated as a competing cause of satisfaction.

per_column.name: clarity_mentions
per_column.rationale: Candidate cause (clarity of instruction) mined from responses; a driver of satisfaction.

per_column.name: workload_mentions
per_column.rationale: Candidate driver mined from text; a competing cause of satisfaction.

per_column.name: primary_driver
per_column.rationale: A pre-computed attribution/label of which factor dominates; it is a derived conclusion, not a treatment or confounder input, and would leak the outcome if used as a predictor.

per_column.name: satisfaction_band
per_column.rationale: Discretisation of the outcome variable; not a cause or confounder.

judge.rationale: The added columns supply plausible candidate TREATMENTS (tech, engagement, clarity, workload mentions extracted from the open responses), so requirement (a) is met. However, requirement (b) is entirely unmet: no CONFOUNDERS are present. A confounder would be a variable that plausibly causes both a mentioned-factor treatment and satisfaction and must be adjusted to avoid biased attribution -- e.g., respondent_role, grade_level, or subject exist in the original table but were NOT surfaced or engineered as adjustment variables, and no new confounders (e.g., prior tech familiarity, class size, remote vs in-person context) were mined. The remaining added columns are all recodings of the outcome (low_satisfaction_flag, satisfaction_band) or a derived attribution label (primary_driver, which is a conclusion/leaky variable). Because the system did not surface any common cause of both treatment and outcome, the causal-attribution claim fails the decisive test.
